# Preface.

## Dear Reader, Honored in Chemical Wisdom and Truth.

It is more superfluous than necessary to have the first class of the present **Touchstone** <note>original: *Probier-Stein*; a stone used to test the purity of gold and silver. Here, it is a metaphor for a book that tests the truth of alchemical claims.</note> reprinted anew, since the same should already be sufficiently well-known; however, because at this time the second class—serving as the *Register of the Sophists* <note>In alchemical context, "sophists" were considered "false chemists" or fraudsters who lacked true spiritual and practical knowledge.</note>—is to be shared and made known to the **Sons of the Alchemical Art of Wisdom**; and since in the meantime various other treatises have come into our hands which belong in the first class; and above all, because this first class, before it could be properly finalized, was published quite prematurely against our knowledge and will, un-

# Preface.

—perfect, without form, and indeed just as the <term>authors</term> <note>original: *Authores*</note> were read and recorded, except that he intended to arrange them alphabetically; it was submitted to print in this state, and therefore it is not only full of <term>errors</term> <note>original: *Errata*</note> and defects, but entirely confused. We find ourselves quite ashamed of it, and so we have taken the effort upon ourselves to search through all authors anew, compared them against the register, improved what was necessary, and brought it into a more convenient form. We have devoted everything to this work that may be edifying to the honored reader and lovers of the **Great Secret Science** <note>original: *geheimen Wissenschafft*; referring here to alchemy and the hermetic arts</note>. We have also entirely omitted the preface and the dialogue of the persons featured therein for the sake of brevity; however, whoever finds interest in those may make use of the first edition.

This is all in the firm hope that it will be well received by our <term>disciples</term> <note>original: *Disciplen*</note>, as sons of the **True Art of Wisdom** <note>original: *wahrhafften Weißheits-Kunst*; a traditional term for the practice of alchemy, implying both chemical and spiritual mastery</note>. ### 2. *Agrippa (Heinrich Cornelius)*

born in *Cologne*, of the family of *Nettesheim*, a learned mind who experienced very wondrous *fates* <note>original Latin: *fata*</note>; for he was a *Secretary* at the Imperial Court; an *Officer* with the *Venetians*; a *Syndic* and *Legate* in *Metz*; a *Physician* in *Freiburg*; the *Personal Physician* to the Queen of *France*, and Imperial *Court Councilor* &c. And yet, fortune would not tolerate him anywhere, but pursued him from one place to another until he gave up his noble spirit. He was a man of high gifts and deep insights; a well-experienced <term>Cabalist</term> <note>A student of the Cabala, a mystical system of interpreting the universe and scripture.</note>, <term>Magus</term> <note>A practitioner of natural or divine magic.</note> and <term>Theosophus</term> <note>A "God-knower" or seeker of divine wisdom through direct experience.</note>; a <term>Mathematicus</term> <note>A mathematician; in this era, the term often encompassed astronomy and astrology.</note>, <term>Astrologus</term> <note>An astrologer.</note> and <term>Alchymist</term> <note>An alchemist.</note>; he was also a possessor of the **Hermetic Secrets**, as his writings sufficiently give to understand. Although he was exposed to many *fates* <note>original: *Fatis*</note>, he was nonetheless a hero in this regard, who knew how to face his changes, shifts, enviers, and envious fortune, to endure it with composure and to hold out against it. But as for him being numbered among the sorcerers and <term>Necromantists</term> <note>Those who purportedly communicate with the spirits of the dead for divination.</note> and held as suspicious, no other cause or ground is known for this than that he wrote a treatise—

of the Touchstone, &c.

written on the *Uncertainty and Vanity of the Sciences and Arts* <note>original: *De incertitudine et vanitate scientiarum atque artium*, Agrippa's famous 1530 critique of the intellectual world</note>, in which he quite sharply attacked the errors and follies of all classes, especially the scholars, because of which they became resentful toward him; Beyond this, in the year 1533, he wrote to his home city regarding Doctor Luther, praising and commending his teachings, while conversely attacking and revealing the malice and abominations of the <term>Clergy</term> <note>original: *Clerisey*</note> there; he also sided with Calvin, and loved those who walked in the secret ways of God and wrote concerning the state of the soul after death. This annoyed his enemies, the Clergy, so much that they pursued him everywhere, labeling him with the name of a heretic and a sorcerer, and would have gladly sent him into the next world; but as God had decreed it, so it had to go. It is dreadful that Protestant teachers do not investigate these matters better, but instead, to please the Papacy, quite blindly and only from hearsay, place such highly blessed men and true <term>Co-Reformers</term> <note>original: *Mit-Reformatores*</note> among the number of heretics. We wish that his writings, some of which also adorn our *Chemical Library*, were all available in the German language, so that they might be shared by everyone. His alchemical writings are not for beginners and the inexperienced.

4. **Brother Albert** of the Carmelite Order, wrote a small <term>little treatise</term> in the form of a dialogue with the spirit *Mercury*, titled *The Dialogue of Mercury and Albert* <note>original: *Colloquium Mercurii & Alberti*</note>, and it is attached to the writings of *Sendivogius* <note>Michael Sendivogius, a famous Polish alchemist and physician</note>. Beginners should not expect to find joy in it, for <term>sophistry</term> <note>original: *Sophisterey*; here meaning deceptive or intentionally confusing language</note> has a large share in its concealment.

# First Part /

[...who lived] in Lüneburg; a precious and zealous soul, and a faithful follower of Jesus Christ. He struggled with earnestness to awaken the poor children of Adam <note>A common theological term for humanity, referring to the shared inheritance of "Original Sin" following the biblical Fall of Man.</note>, and to impress upon them the Fall of their father and the wrath of God over sin. To this end, he composed various quite magnificent writings, one of which is *True Christianity* <note>original: "wahre Christenthum"; This 1605 book by Johann Arndt (1555–1621) became one of the most influential works of Protestant devotion, emphasizing personal piety over rigid dogma.</note>. In this work, he reveals all the abominations of sin, the curse, damnation, and the wrath of God; but in contrast, he also profoundly presented the blessed return, repentance, conversion, grace, love, and the salvation of the godly.

In his fourth and fifth books of this *True Christianity* concerning Creation, he allowed the <term>first matter of the philosopher's stone</term> <note>original: "primam materiam lapidis Philosophorum"; the fundamental, raw substance required to begin the alchemical "Great Work" of transformation.</note> and its entire preparation to flow in so gracefully, sweetly, and pleasantly, that it will not be easily noticed by anyone who is not already a connoisseur of nature and its works. Consequently, beginners will find no earthly light in those passages, because he stood and wrote within a divine light. 

But regarding the salvation of mankind, he calls out loudly as if with a trumpet, and reaches out with both arms to lead the poor sinner back to God through Christ. He did not say, as one did recently who believed he was not being shown enough honor: "You may indeed look upon us as ministers and servants of the Gospel, but know..."

# of the Touchstone / etc.

When a servant or minister has a high lord whom he serves, such a servant or minister is also due great honor and respect. However, **JESUS Christ** says that whoever wishes to be the greatest among His own should be the servant of all, just as He himself has done. He says further: My sheep hear my voice, and I give them eternal life, and whoever does not deny himself cannot be his disciple; likewise: He did not have even so much as a place where He could lay his head. If the **LORD** thus laments the lack of external things, what honor then is due to the minister or servant? Or, is such a <term>sermon-hack</term> <note>original: "Postillen-Reuter"; literally a "postil-rider," a derogatory term for a preacher who simply recites or copies from standard sermon collections (postils) rather than speaking from genuine spiritual experience.</note> also to be counted among the disciples and apostles of Jesus? But let everyone take heed of themselves. Our blessed **Arndt** teaches that we must learn to truly know ourselves, so that we may become ashamed of ourselves, enter into the true nothingness <note>A mystical concept referring to "Gelassenheit" or self-abandonment, where one empties the self to be filled by God.</note>, be born anew therein, and take on a new form in **Christ**—yes, so that it may be revealed in us that we are in **Christ** and **Christ** is in us. We recommend the writings of this blessed man to all souls yearning for salvation.

[The House] of Light / which in the year 1690 was translated from English into German by **Johann Lang** in **Hamburg** and brought to print. However, justice requires that we also say in our **defense** <term>Defension: a formal legal or academic defense of one’s position</term>, that at the same time and as a **manifesto** made public in our writings, it was stated that our works were not written for the highly learned, for the **philosophers** <term>Weltweisen: literally "world-wise," a term often used for secular or academic philosophers</term>, for those **powerful in languages**, or for the **"great spirits"** and **"strong spirits"** <note>original: "Grands Esprits & Esprits forts," French terms referring to the witty intellectuals and skeptical free-thinkers of the era</note>. # of the Touchstone / etc.

...should have, that the Mr. Author <note>Thomas Vaughan, writing under the pseudonym Eugenius Philalethes</note> saw fit to name it so, and that a Mr. Lang followed him in translating it thus into German. It is true that *Aula* <note>Latin: court or hall</note> means the court, or better the fore-court, and as the English understand it, it means the gallery of the Royal Palace. But even though *Aula Lucis* <note>Latin: Court of Light</note> means the court or fore-court of light, it is nonetheless true that the Mr. Author also added "or the House of Light," and as it is called in the English language, **House of Light**. These two terms can quite easily stand together and do not contradict one another, since the Mr. Author considered the subject he is dealing with—namely the *First Matter* <term>primam Materiam: the "First Matter," the primordial, formless substance that alchemists sought as the starting point for the Great Work</term>—far too important and lofty to have assigned it only a single place. For this reason, he named two principal places for it: namely the court, which is the Royal Fore-court, and then the house, which is the Royal Palace. As the Mr. Author himself says on page 25: "The matter, as I previously indicated, is the House of Light." Elsewhere he says that it is the "Throne of the Crystalline Light." Consequently, we see that the Mr. Author has assigned this so noble, magnificent, and majestic light two residences for its proper—

**57. Flamel, (Nicholas)** a former scribe in Paris, as he himself testifies, who was initially of modest means but became so rich through the Art of Alchemy that he built quite notable hospitals, churches, and chapels, as even his enemies and the enemies of Alchemy must confess. Nevertheless, some wish to turn this honest man into a thief of public funds <note>original: *Renten-Dieb*. Literally a "rent-thief," this refers to accusations that Flamel embezzled tax revenues or state pensions to account for his sudden wealth.</note>, as if he had stolen so many thousands. 81. **Hortulanus**, the Gardener, an Englishman, wrote a **commentary** <note>original: *Commentarium*</note> on the **Emerald Tablet of Hermes**, with which he did beginners a great service of love and lit a magnificent light so that they do not stumble at the entrance of the palace. Beginners should therefore make use of his benevolent spirit; he has done his part, as befits a true **Hermetic** <note>original: *Hermetico*; a follower of the teachings of Hermes Trismegistus</note>. It was published in Vienna in 1709 and also appears in the <term>Theatrum Chemicum: a massive and famous multi-volume compendium of alchemical writings first published in the 17th century</term>.

82. **One is my Dove** <note>original: *Eine ist meine Duben*; a reference to the Song of Solomon 6:9, often used in alchemy to symbolize the "White Stone" or the purity of the work</note>. A small treatise or secret manuscript, so named by one of our dear and loyal friends, who first received the noble pearl, the royal jewel (the highest <term>Arcanum: a deep secret or mystery, specifically the ultimate medicinal or transformative secret sought by alchemists</term>), as a treasure of all treasures from the well-born Lord Pru-von-Pru. He composed it into a concise manuscript under the title *One is my Dove*, that is, a divine mystery of all mysteries, called the **Philosopher’s Stone** <note>original: *lapis Philosophorum*</note>. It is written in his own hand and likewise adorns our **Chemical Library** to his everlasting praise. This noble manuscript is without a key <note>A "key" refers to an explanation or code used to decipher the allegorical language of the text</note>, and it is kept as a precious treasure, reserved for dear friends to see.

86. **Kempis**, (**Thomas à**)

The viewing lasted for several days. On a Sunday, he came once again: the mining lads <note>original: "Berg-Knaben"; refers to the young apprentices and laborers in the mines</note> and the coarse rabble surrounded him, took him for a **spy** and such things, and **attacked** him with stones, clumps of earth, and sticks. ### 112. **Morning Glow**, (the rising) *Rising Dawn* <note>original Latin: *Aurora consurgens*</note>, is a small treatise that is attached to the *Assembly of the Philosophers* <note>original Latin: *Turba Philosophorum*; one of the oldest and most influential Latin alchemical texts, presented as a debate between ancient philosophers.</note> in the *art of making gold* <note>original Latin: *in arte aurifera*</note>. It contains good teachings, but it is not intended for beginners.

### 113. **Morienus**, is said to have been a hermit in Jerusalem who possessed quite exceptional gifts of wisdom. He was, as his work shows, a pious man who conducted himself as a true hermit and one betrothed to the **LORD**, and not like so many in today's times, who unfortunately have much in common with thieves and murderers—those who are merely swallowers of good wine, beer, and brandy. Instead, our blessed *Morienus* showed through both his teaching and his life how one can be pleasing to **GOD** in life and in death. He was a possessor of the **Philosopher's Stone**, and held quite a different *perspective* <note>original: *Sentiment*</note> than other ancient *writers* <note>original Latin: *Scribenten*</note>, because he handled the entire work with great love and guided his followers as if by the hand to show them the mystery. You beginners, hold him dear! His *treatise* <note>original: *Tractat*</note> is located in the second part of the *Assembly of the Philosophers* <note>original: *Turba*</note>.

### 117. **Padua**, (**Johannes de**)

124. **Plato** (not *Platony*, as it appeared in the first edition, for which we were capriciously mocked by a Pole as if we did not even understand basic orthography—though it remains unknown whether the author, the scribe, or the printer bears the blame for that error.) He is said to have been born in Athens, specifically 325 years after the founding of the city of Rome. He was initially a painter, then a poet, and finally a philosopher, becoming one of the most learned men of Asia and Greece. His **natural light** <term>natural light: often referred to as the *Lumen Naturae*, this is the innate human intellect or wisdom that allows one to understand the physical and spiritual world without divine revelation</term> and temperament led him so high that he endeavored to research everything and to converse with all the wise men of his time. It is even said that he read the writings of **Moses** and loved them, for which reason he is called the **Athenian Moses** <note>original: *Athenische Moses*. This refers to the historical claim by thinkers like Numenius of Apamea that Plato's philosophy was essentially a Greek version of Mosaic law: "What is Plato but Moses speaking Attic Greek?"</note>. He also demonstrated a special love for posterity; for this reason, in his writings (which were translated into Latin and printed in the year 1602), he provided many distinct signs of his wisdom regarding **Alchemy**. These signs are intended to guide a person through the difficulties that may be encountered on the **Hermetic wandering-roads** <note>This phrase refers to the metaphorical and often confusing journey a student takes to master the "Hermetic" or alchemical arts.</note>. However, he who does not already hold the **Key of Hermes** <term>Key of Hermes: a symbolic or actual secret principle required to decode the allegories and "blind" instructions found in alchemical texts</term> in his hands will find little of edification within them.

135. **The Knightly War (Ancient)**
or **Hermetic Triumph**, together with the dialogue between **Eudoxus** and **Pyrophilus**, and the Letter to the true disciples of **Hermes** <note>original: "Hermetis"</note>, which consists of six keys and flowed from a single pen. ### 138. Rosicrucian (Christian)
<note>Referring to Christian Rosenkreutz, the legendary founder of the Rosicrucian Order</note>

His *Chymical Wedding* <note>original: "Chimische Hochzeit," referring to the famous 1616 book *Chymische Hochzeit Christiani Rosencreutz anno 1459*</note> is a parabolic and veiled piece of writing, such that the author himself, were he present today, would likely not know what he intended to say by it. It has been given this place in our list not for its own **merits**, but because of the praise that is commonly bestowed upon it; for it is useful neither to beginners nor to anyone else. The author possessed no Christian love at all, and perhaps even knew or understood nothing. It is a pity for the time lost upon it.

### 140. Rosinus

A highly learned and highly famous man, who was a collaborator on the **Great Universal Building** <note>A metaphorical term for the collective endeavor of alchemical knowledge and the perfection of nature</note>, and who treated the **Work** <note>The "Work" (Opus) refers to the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone</note> in several writings, of which we have a fragment in the German language; however, it is not suitable for beginners. When we, with the best possible **goodwill**, without intentions of profit or interest, without seeking honor or favor, yet with unbelievable toil and difficulty alone—on the one hand to be useful and to serve our neighbor and the lover of the high truth, and on the other hand to free the high wisdom and hidden science from the burden of the **Babylonian** and **Egyptian** sorcerers <note>The author refers to the ancient roots of alchemy, suggesting that "true" wisdom has been obscured by the confusing or "magical" writings of these ancient traditions.</note>—have prepared this **Touchstone** <term>Touchstone: (German: Probier-Stein) A tool used to test the purity of precious metals; here it refers to the book itself as a standard for judging alchemical texts.</term>.

Since the world has already been embittered toward **Alchemy** for some centuries, having delved into it so deeply, consumed its time very uselessly therein, spent its health, honor, fortune, and credit upon it, and yet could find nothing sustainable; it has become very indignant and has attacked both the high truth itself as well as the persons of the practitioners. And yet, we presently take the liberty to reveal to you the ground and the foundation of why you are not capable of finding the way, that

15. **Basilius Valentinus.** <note>Basilius Valentinus was a legendary 15th-century Benedictine monk and alchemist. While he is a pillar of the tradition, modern scholars believe the name was a pseudonym for the publisher Johann Thölde (c. 1565–1614).</note> That this author was one of the most honest writers, we have shown in the first part; however, some have had the audacity to attribute other, forged writings to him, which are nothing but true slanders and dishonorable, thievish tricks, through which they have sought to make this honest man’s name stink before the world. He certainly never wrote anything of the kind in his life and would have been ashamed to leave behind for posterity such honorless, God-forsaken, sophistical—one might even say, abominable <note>original: *Sodomitsche* (Sodomitic); used here as a severe moral condemnation of fraudulent texts.</note>—pieces. His upright way of life and his conscience would not have permitted him to describe such wicked rogue-tricks, through which so many people could be deprived of their property. They are therefore by no means the work of **Valentinus**, nor of any other **Chemical Adept**, <term>Adept: A person who has successfully achieved the "Great Work" of alchemy, specifically the creation of the Philosopher's Stone.</term> but are rather sophistical lie-writings against which honest souls should guard themselves. They deserve to be burned by the hand of the executioner and are as follows:

a. **Basilius Valentinus’s** Practical Methods of **Particular Processes**. <term>Particulars: In alchemy, "particular" processes were those that only achieved a partial transformation of metals (e.g., turning a small amount of silver into gold) rather than the "Universal" transformation promised by the Philosopher's Stone. They were often viewed with suspicion as potential scams.</term>
b. The same author’s Revelation of Hidden Practical Methods. <note>original: *Ejusdem Offenbahrung verborgener Hand-Griffen*</note>
c. The same author’s Fifth Book of his Last Testament. See **Cardilucius**. <note>Johann Hiskia Cardilucius (1638–1710) was a German physician and chemist who edited many of these works; the author here refers the reader to Cardilucius’s own critiques or editions.</note>

### 29. Buddeus, (Johann Franz)
*Doctor of Sacred Theology* <note>original: "SS. Theol. Doctor"</note> and *Full Public Professor* <note>original: "Professor publ. Ord."</note>, *Historical and Political Investigation of Alchemy*. The author is well-known as a very learned man; he exerted great effort to discover the true *Hermetic science* <note>original: "Hermeticam"; refers to the secret arts of alchemy and philosophy attributed to Hermes Trismegistus.</note> and to that end leafed through many authors, as the present work demonstrates. One can say that he investigated matters from the ground up, so to speak, and believed for certain that the Hermetic science was truth; therefore, he also wrote his historical and political investigation so that he might lay it out clearly and as if in the light for the rational world, showing impartially how he found such things. For this work, then, as well as for the author's great effort, we hold a special *esteem* <note>original: "Æstime"</note> and include him here without prejudice to his honor. We would have placed him in the first class <note>The author divides his bibliography into "classes" or categories of quality; the first class is reserved for the most authentic masters of alchemy.</note> if certain passages had not been cited; for it is one thing to describe a matter *historically* <note>original: "historice"</note>, and quite another to describe it according to nature and for the purpose of instruction.

If it had been found false—as in the highest truth it is—it would have been immediately consigned to the fire. Therefore, let no one be swayed by grand titles, as fraudsters strive to invent all kinds of such processes. This process deserves nothing else than to be handed over to the fire.

64. **Secret of Life and the Multiplication of all Things**, also ***Key of the Hermetic Philosophers*** <note>original Latin: "Clavis Philosophorum Hermeticorum"</note>, are two small treatises that were printed in **Dresden** in the year 1748. 65. **Geißler, (Friedrich)** published a treatise in the year 1683, ***Tree of Life***; that is, a thorough report on **Potable Gold** <note>original Latin: "Auro potabili"; a legendary medicinal elixir made from dissolved gold</note> and the **Philosopher's Stone**. He understood not the slightest bit of the **Hermetic Philosophy**, and his **Potable Gold** is as far removed from the truth as **arsenic** is from **sugar**.

### 75. **Hermes Trismegistus**, his *Knowledge of Nature* / published in the year 1706.

Therefore, the author did not act very wisely with this little treatise by bestowing such a title upon it. As for the little work itself, we do not know what purpose it is meant to serve, or what great wisdom is to be gained from it? Consequently, it is of no use to the lovers of the Hermetic sciences.

**81. Idea**, (a two-fold medicinal work) concerning that universal plague, Greed <note>original: "Geitz"</note>, which appeared in the year 1707. The author is unknown, but his surviving writings testify that he was a simpleton squeezer <term>Quetscher | A derogatory term used by serious alchemists for "puffers" or charlatans who tried to "squeeze" results out of base materials through brute force or incorrect heat, rather than following natural processes.</term> who would have liked to catch fish, but did not want to get his feet wet; for he desired that an Adept <term>Adeptus | A master of alchemy who has supposedly achieved the "Great Work" and created the Philosopher's Stone.</term> should come and shove roasted pigeons into his mouth <note>A German idiom referring to someone who is lazy and expects to be fed success without any effort.</note>. Like the Egyptians, he makes flesh his arm and withdraws his heart from the Lord <note>A reference to Jeremiah 17:5, "Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his arm, whose heart turns away from the Lord."</note>, whereas we ought first to seek GOD, and only then seek gold.

**82. Ignis perpetuus** <note>original Latin: "Perpetual Fire."</note>. The author is said to have been a Carthusian father <note>A monk of the Carthusian Order, who lived in strict silence and isolation; the author suggests such a lifestyle is incompatible with the laboratory work of alchemy.</note>, though this is to be doubted, as these people can or should hardly burden themselves with such things. But let him be who he may, he was an arch-sophistical scribbler and squeezer who hatched nothing but argo-chemical <term>argochimistisch | A term for fraudulent or counterfeit alchemy, derived from "Argo" (likely referencing the ship of the Argonauts or simply implying "work" that is deceptive) and "chemistry."</term> deceit, as the work clearly proves.

83. **Labyrinths** <note>original: "Irrgängen"</note>, (A Treatise on Alchemy), which is printed alongside the writings of Hollandus <note>Isaac Hollandus and his son were 15th-century Dutch alchemists whose works were widely read and often imitated or forged in later centuries.</note>, and was also recently published in Vienna. 87. **Theodor Kerkinger** was a learned man and a Doctor of Medicine <note>original: "Doctor Medicinæ"</note> in Amsterdam who possessed great knowledge; however, in **Hermetic Alchemy** <term>original Latin: "Alchimia Hermetica"; the philosophical and spiritual study of chemical transformation</term> he was ignorant. 152. **Schütz**, (**Johann**) Little Treatise on the **Philosopher's Stone**, which was printed in Hamburg in the year 1682; the author is not further known to us. 153. **Schwertzer**, (**Sebald**) his chemical writings were published anew in the year 1718. It is world-famous who the author was, and history reports (though this is to be doubted, because Kunckel <note>Referring to Johann von Löwenstern-Kunckel, a famous 17th-century chemist and glassmaker.</note> tells it quite differently in his *Laboratorio*) that he was a **manslayer**, who received his tincture from a **Son of Art** <note>original: *Filio artis*; a traditional alchemical term for a true initiate or adept who has mastered the craft.</note>, traveled around the world, and performed great feats, yet was never able to make a tincture himself. ### of the Touchstone, etc.

O wretched people! For God’s sake, consider all these minor representations, which are but a shadow compared to the reality itself. Remember, Adam committed only one sin, and yet the wrath of God flared up over the entire world; consider then what sin truly is, and what it entails? Consider that after sin follows wrath and punishment. 

Consider and weigh this: when God sends a heavy thunderstorm, where it flashes and cracks and here and there a bolt of lightning strikes, how people are terrified, trembling, and anxious—yes, how they even howl and cry out as their evil consciences convict them of their perverse deeds and the terrifying wrath of God. Yet such a storm only passes by, and often does not last even an hour. 

Think then how it shall be in the places of eternity, where the wrath of God will rage and rave over the sinner in the same manner without ceasing, and for all eternity.
